categories.main_business_segments: Apellis Pharmaceuticals operates primarily in two business segments: rare disease (notably hematology and nephrology) and ophthalmology. Its commercial products are EMPAVELI (systemic pegcetacoplan) for paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) and SYFOVRE (intravitreal pegcetacoplan) for geographic atrophy (GA) secondary to age-related macular degeneration. The company is also advancing pegcetacoplan for additional indications and developing new complement-targeting therapies.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Apellis's core technology is based on the inhibition of the complement system at the level of C3, the central protein in the complement cascade. Its lead compound, pegcetacoplan, is a compstatin analog administered either systemically (subcutaneous injection) or intravitreally (eye injection). Manufacturing involves chemical synthesis, purification, and formulation, with production outsourced to third-party contract manufacturers under cGMP standards.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The primary customers are healthcare providers treating patients with rare hematologic and nephrologic diseases (such as PNH, CAD, C3G, and HSCT-TMA), as well as ophthalmologists and retina specialists treating geographic atrophy. End markets include hospitals, specialty clinics, and specialty pharmacies serving patients with high unmet medical needs.
categories.geographic_coverage: Apellis commercializes EMPAVELI in the United States and, through its partner Sobi, in Europe, the UK, Australia, Saudi Arabia, and other international markets. SYFOVRE is approved and launched in the United States, with regulatory submissions underway or planned in the EU, Canada, Switzerland, Australia, and the UK. The company maintains a global clinical and commercial footprint.
categories.supply_chain_position: Apellis operates downstream in the biopharmaceutical supply chain, focusing on late-stage development, commercialization, and marketing of finished pharmaceutical products. It relies on third-party contract manufacturers for raw materials, drug substance, and finished product, and partners with specialty distributors and pharmacies for product distribution.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic focus is on expanding the clinical utility of complement inhibition, particularly at the C3 level, across rare diseases, ophthalmology, and neurology. R&D priorities include label expansion for pegcetacoplan, development of new complement-targeting modalities (e.g., siRNA combinations, bispecific inhibitors), and gene-editing collaborations (notably with Beam Therapeutics). Apellis aims to establish best-in-class therapies and broaden its pipeline through internal innovation and partnerships.
categories.revenue_model: Apellis generates revenue primarily through product sales of EMPAVELI and SYFOVRE, supplemented by milestone payments, royalties, and cost reimbursements from its collaboration with Sobi for ex-US commercialization. The company also receives development funding and milestone payments from research collaborations.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Key competitors include AstraZeneca (Soliris, Ultomiris), Novartis (iptacopan), Iveric Bio (avacincaptad pegol), Sanofi (sutimlimab-jome), and others developing complement inhibitors or alternative therapies for PNH, GA, and related indications. Apellis positions itself as a leader in C3 inhibition, offering differentiated, first-in-class or best-in-class therapies in markets with high unmet need and limited competition, especially in GA where SYFOVRE is the first approved treatment.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2022, Apellis had $551.8 million in cash and equivalents, with net product revenue of $65.1 million from EMPAVELI in 2022 and $80.2 million since launch. The company reported significant net losses ($652.2 million in 2022) and anticipates continued losses as it invests in commercialization and R&D. Apellis is transitioning from a development-stage to a commercial-stage company, with expected revenue growth driven by new product launches and label expansions.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Apellis’s value proposition centers on its unique approach to broad complement inhibition at C3, enabling treatment of diseases with high unmet need where existing therapies are limited or ineffective. Pegcetacoplan offers differentiated clinical benefits, such as improved control of both intravascular and extravascular hemolysis in PNH and the first-ever approved therapy for GA. The company emphasizes patient-centric solutions, flexible dosing, and the potential for best-in-class efficacy and safety.
